gap: None of the results ChatGPT got puts these watches side by side by golf-GPS hours. They compare 21 vs 11 vs 10 days of smartwatch battery. Measured by GPS hours, Garmin's own figures put the vívoactive 5 and vívoactive 6 (17 h all-systems, 21 h GPS-only) above the golf-only Approach S44 (15 h), so the fitness watches last 3–4 four-and-a-half-hour rounds per charge against about 3 for the S44.
standout_why: Cited rivals: Garmin's S44/S50 press release, OutdoorGearLab, WIRED, Garmin's golf Which Watch compare page (cited in both later chats) and the vívoactive 5 manual's golf pages. The press release does give the S44's 15 h GPS figure. The vívoactive 5 battery manual page (rank 2, not cited) has 17 h and 21 h but nothing on the S44. Panxis (not cited) gives only the S44 and its own guess of 2.5–3 rounds. No page puts the vívoactive 6 GPS hours next to the S44's, or turns them into rounds per charge. ChatGPT's own table footnote admits its battery column is smartwatch days, 'not continuous golf GPS use'. So rivals have parts but not the side-by-side comparison. It falls short of a 2 because the Amazfit Balance 2 row, ChatGPT's first pick in one chat, can't be normalised from a page I opened.
decides: This confirms the vívoactive 5 and 6 over the Approach S44 for a golf-plus-fitness buyer. The vívoactive models are rated for more on-course GPS time than the S44, and they add wrist heart rate and sleep tracking, which the S44 doesn't have. The vívoactive 6 manual's golf menu also has Hazards, Layups, PinPointer and View Green, so ChatGPT calling its golf 'basic' undersells it. The Balance 2's 21-day headline is a smartwatch figure and can't be ranked against Garmin's GPS hours until Amazfit's GPS-mode numbers are sourced.
